summary: feat(pagination): capture the Fiken-Api-* result-count headers and use them for provenance, a sync completeness check and doctor (issue #15)
reason: Fiken's list endpoints answer with a bare JSON array and no envelope, so the only completeness signal on the wire is the response header block Fiken-Api-Page / -Page-Size / -Page-Count / -Result-Count (spec.yaml:247-255, declared on 27 of the 40 list operations). The printed client discarded resp.Header except Content-Type, so nothing - not sync, not doctor, not a paginated read's provenance envelope - could tell how many rows a resource holds or whether a page was the last one. That is why issue #12 (the page-1 skip that landed 477 of 577 accounts) went unnoticed for the life of the mirror. The capture is a context-value sink in the hand-authored internal/client/page_info.go (PageInfo, PageInfoSink, NewPageInfoContext, ParsePageInfo) so the generated request path needs exactly one line - capturePageInfo(ctx, resp.Header) in the success branch of (*Client).doInternal - and no signature anywhere changes: paginatedGet and its 27 generated call sites, and both sync walkers' `c.Get` interface, are untouched. The sink keeps the FIRST response that carried headers (Result-Count is the collection total on every page) and Reset starts a new collection. Consumers: (1) resolvePaginatedReadWithStrategy installs a sink and each live return passes the provenance through attachPageInfo, which fills the new optional DataProvenance.ResultCount/PageCount pointers; wrapWithProvenance emits meta.result_count and meta.page_count only when present, so an absent header is never published as a zero count. (2) syncResource and syncDependentResource compare the rows they landed against Fiken-Api-Result-Count and emit one sync_anomaly with reason result_count_mismatch per (company, resource) when they differ; the comparison is skipped for a walk that was resumed from a stored cursor or exited early (--max-pages / --latest-only, stuck cursor, non-JSON body, fetch or upsert error), because such a walk is short by construction and says nothing about completeness. (3) sync_state gains a nullable result_count column (declared in the CREATE for a fresh DB and in backfillColumns for an existing one - backfillColumns runs before the CREATE statements, so a fresh DB needs both) written by the new SaveSyncResultCount and read by SyncResultCount, and doctor's cache report adds result_count to a resource entry when one was recorded. The recorded number is only written when it is on the same scale as sync_state.total_count, which is the mirror-wide row count (syncStateTotalCount): headers present for every parent walked, no early exit, and no --company scope. A --company or capped run leaves the previously recorded value alone rather than overwriting it with a partial sum. NULL result_count means 'no run ever saw the header', which is not the same claim as zero rows - hence PageInfo.Present / HasResultCount and the *int provenance fields. Review follow-ups on the first landing, all four of them about what the recorded number MEANS. (a) Windowed pulls: once issue #13 fills the temporal-filter mapping, a --since or watermark run sends lastModifiedGe and Fiken answers with the Result-Count of the FILTERED set, so recording it would overwrite the full-collection 577 with 3 and doctor would report rows 577 / result_count 3. syncResultCountComparable therefore became shouldRecordResultCount(seen, truncated, windowed) and both walkers pass whether their request carried the since parameter (effectiveSince / depSinceTS, both already emptied when the endpoint declares no temporal filter). The per-pull mismatch comparison still runs for a windowed pull — header and rows describe the same filtered set — only the persisted value is skipped. syncSinceParamFor / syncSinceParamResolver is the seam that mapping will plug into (the generated syncResourceSinceParam switch is empty because the spec does not declare the parameter) and is what lets a test drive the windowed path today. (b) The rows side of the comparison was the sum of UpsertBatch's `stored`, which counts ITEMS with an extractable id, not rows: the same id served twice across a page boundary counted twice (false anomaly on a perfect mirror) and two items collapsing onto one storage key also counted twice, which HID the issue #12 failure class (mirror short, counters agreeing). Both walkers now accumulate a landedIDs set of DISTINCT storage keys — store.StorageKeyOf is the only way to compute the key a row lands under, since resourceStorageID is unexported and the key is id-plus-parent — and that distinct count is what the anomaly reports as rows. The set keeps insertion order because issue #17 (deletion detection) reads it. (c) doctor selected result_count with a per-row s.SyncResultCount(rtype) call INSIDE the open rows.Next() loop; the pool is capped at two connections, so a Store shared with a running sync stalled. It is now one column in the outer query, scanned as sql.NullInt64. Store.SyncResultCount stays as the read half of SaveSyncResultCount (tests use it) but has no production caller. (d) page_count was gated on `> 0` while result_count was gated on presence, so an empty collection's Page-Count: 0 was silently dropped; PageInfo gained HasPageCount and both are presence-gated. (*Client).GetPage was removed: the context sink IS the read path and a second cache-bypassing entry point had no caller.

validated_outcome: make check green (go vet ./..., go test ./..., scripts/check-boundaries.sh). Hand-authored tests: internal/client/page_info_test.go drives an httptest server that sets the four headers - TestSinkedGet_ParsesFikenPaginationHeaders parses {0 100 3 250} alongside the body, TestSinkedGet_NoHeadersIsAbsentNotZero keeps a header-less response at the zero value, TestPageInfoSink_KeepsFirstResponseAndResets pins first-page-wins and Reset, TestPageInfoSink_NilAndUnsetContextAreNoOps keeps the patched doInternal line harmless without a sink. internal/cli/pagination_headers_test.go extends the pageServer harness from pagination_zero_based_test.go with the header block: meta.result_count/page_count appear on a paginated read (single page and --all) and are omitted without headers; a pull of 150 rows against a claimed Result-Count of 250 emits exactly one result_count_mismatch (result_count 250, rows 150) on both the flat and the dependent walker, a complete 250-row pull emits none and records 250, a --max-pages 1 walk emits none and records nothing, and doctor's cache report shows result_count for a resource that has one and omits it for one that does not (HOME redirected to a temp dir so the real mirror is untouched). No live API call was made. Review follow-up run: make check green; go test -race ./internal/client/... ./internal/cli/... green. Added TestParsePageInfo_ZeroCountsArePresent and TestPaginatedRead_EmptyCollectionPublishesZeroCounts (Page-Count: 0 is published, not dropped), TestSyncResource_DuplicateIDAcrossPagesIsNotAnAnomaly (251 items, 250 distinct ids, claimed 250 -> no anomaly; pre-fix: one), TestSyncResource_CollapsedStorageKeysEmitAnomaly (250 items collapsing to 249 rows, claimed 250 -> one anomaly with rows 249; pre-fix: silent), TestShouldRecordResultCount (the pure decision) and TestSyncResource_WindowedPullKeepsRecordedResultCount (a windowed short pull still emits the mismatch but leaves the recorded 577 alone; the unwindowed control records). The two GetPage tests became TestSinkedGet_* and drive (*Client).Get under a sink, which is the production path. Every new test was checked red against the pre-fix code. No live API call was made.
